content: The test image shows white cottony/fluffy mycelial growth on the stem and pod area of a soybean plant. This is strongly suggestive of White Mold. Let me check reference images across my top candidates.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Dense white cottony/fluffy mycelial growth wrapped tightly around a soybean stem and pod. Pod appears shriveled/collapsing. Background shows yellowing leaves.
- **White Mold ref 1** (Dise_133): Later-stage White Mold — bleached stem with black sclerotia embedded. Different stage but same disease.
- **White Mold ref 2** (Dise_291): Collapsed wilted stems from White Mold — stem rot/dieback pattern.
- **Powdery Mildew ref**: Thin white powder on leaf surfaces at field scale — not matching.
- **Downy Mildew ref**: Yellow spots on leaf surfaces — not matching.

The white fluffy mycelium on stem/pod is the hallmark sign of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum* (White Mold / Sclerotinia stem rot). No other class produces this dense cottony growth on stems/pods.
